en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Neptune City, Monmouth County, New Jersey, July 1890, Sheet 21

sheet-9999997.description: Sheet 21 of the Sanborn-Perris New Jersey Coast map, dated July 1890 and drawn at 60 feet to an inch, titled Neptune City. It covers the south end of what is now Bradley Beach, between the area lettered Bradley Beach at the top of the sheet and the tidewater of Sylvan Lake along the bottom. Ocean Avenue, 60 feet wide, runs down the left side, with Pacific and Atlantic Avenues parallel to it further east; Greenwood, Monmouth and Burlington Avenues, each 50 feet wide, cross them. The sheet is turned on the page, with north toward the upper left as the compass rose shows. Twelve numbered blocks are laid out in narrow lots, most still vacant; the buildings drawn are mostly frame dwellings with outbuildings and sheds. Named premises include the Hotel Avon at the corner of Ocean and Greenwood Avenues, a bottling works lettered M. Barreet, bottler, with a storage shed on the same block, the Woolley Bros. livery stables on the block between Pacific and Atlantic Avenues north of Monmouth Avenue, and the Avon Bottling Co. south of Burlington Avenue near Pacific Avenue. West of Ocean Avenue only the edges of blocks 1 and 6 are drawn, with a few scattered buildings. The southern blocks run down to an irregular shoreline, and Ocean Avenue crosses an arm of the lake at the bottom left. The sheet carries its own key to symbols, a compass rose and a scale bar, and lot numbers along every frontage.
notes: Ocean Avenue on the sheet is today's Main Street (NJ 71) in Bradley Beach; today's Ocean Avenue runs along the beach further east.
Greenwood Avenue is today's Evergreen Avenue.
Burlington Avenue is drawn continuing west to Ocean Avenue (Main Street).
The bottler's name is printed M. Barreet.
Junctions of Main Street with Evergreen and Monmouth Avenues were left out of the fit: the sheet draws them about 15 m further apart than the modern junctions, residuals 4.7 and 5.4 m.

Single sheet, printed number 21 of the New Jersey Coast map series, July 1890, scale 60 ft to an inch, turned about 16 degrees (north to upper left). Shows the blocks between Greenwood (now Evergreen), Monmouth and Burlington Avenues and Ocean (now Main Street), Pacific and Atlantic Avenues, down to the north shore of Sylvan Lake; today the south end of Bradley Beach. One part; key table and title cartouche notched out of the mask.
